prompt: I just fixed a bug in our auth service. Expired JWTs were still being accepted because the check compared the issued-at (`iat`) field instead of the expiry (`exp`) field, so any token that had ever been valid kept working forever. The fixed file is token.py (it lives at services/auth/token.py in the repo). Write me a good git commit message for this change. Save the final commit message to commit_msg.txt.

assertions.text: Subject line does NOT start with a conventional-commits type prefix (fix:, feat:, chore:, docs:, refactor:, etc.)
Subject line is scope-first (starts with an area like 'auth:' or 'services/auth:')
Subject line is in imperative mood (e.g. 'Reject'/'Check'/'Compare', not 'Fixed'/'Fixes')
Subject line is roughly 50 characters or fewer
There is a blank line separating the subject from the body
The body explains the why: expired tokens were wrongly accepted because the wrong field (iat vs exp) was compared
